steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Martin wound the clockwork every night at dusk. Had done so for thirty-one years.

The night the storm came, the mechanism jammed. He climbed the stairs anyway — eighty-two steps — and held a lantern to the glass himself, turning slowly, arms burning, until the freighter found the channel and passed safely into harbor.

In the morning, the captain sent up a bottle of whiskey.

Martin sent back a note: *"Just doing what the light does. Somebody has to stand still so others can find their way."*

He wound the clockwork. He climbed the stairs. The sea kept its secrets. The ships came home.
